title: Finite-free coefficient bases and the chain-level sections-tensor comparison at the point
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and finite extensions $E\subset L$ of $\Ql$ inside $\Qlb$, with valuation rings $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $d=[L:E]$, and $R_F=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,s}$ for $F=E,L$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Sections mean evaluation at the final object $s\to s$ of $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$. Constant values give ring isomorphisms $\mathcal O_F\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(s,R_F)$, compatible with coefficient inclusions and with every finite quotient projection. The $R_E$-module sheaf $R_L$ has a basis $b_1,\ldots,b_d$ whose global sections, under these isomorphisms, are an $\mathcal O_E$-basis of $\mathcal O_L$.

For every sheaf $F$ of $R_E$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the balanced map
$$\theta_F:\Gamma(s,F)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L\longrightarrow\Gamma(s,F\otimes_{R_E}R_L),\qquad n\otimes a\longmapsto n\otimes a_s,$$
where $a_s$ is the constant-value section and the tensor on the right is the image under sheafification [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], is an $\mathcal O_L$-linear isomorphism, natural in $F$. Under the coordinate isomorphism $F\otimes_{R_E}R_L\cong F^{\oplus d}$, given locally by $f\otimes\sum_i r_i b_i\mapsto(r_if)_i$, $\theta_F$ is the identity on $\Gamma(s,F)^{\oplus d}$; its inverse sends $(n_i)_i$ to $\sum_i n_i\otimes b_i$. The map $\theta_F$ itself is independent of the chosen basis and uniquely determined by its pure-tensor formula. Both $F\mapsto F\otimes_{R_E}R_L$ and $N\mapsto N\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L$ are additive exact functors (exactness of the sheaf functor is detected after restriction to $R_E$). Applied termwise, the maps $\theta_F$ commute with differentials and give natural isomorphisms of cochain complexes. No discreteness of $R_F$ or sectionwise formula for arbitrary sheaf tensor products is assumed.

source.place: Lemmas 4.2.12 and 6.8.2(1), pp. 58-59; explicit common-global-basis sections calculation extracted from old proof steps 1-2 of lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension, supporting the final paragraph of def-weil-finite-coefficient-point

proof.text: For $H=E,L$ put $A_{H,n}=\mathcal O_H/\varpi_H^n$. These rings are finite by the coefficient convention. Apply [lem-pur-proetale-finite-constant-sections] to $X=V=s$: a function from the singleton underlying space of $s$ to $A_{H,n}$ is specified by its constant value. Thus $\Gamma(s,(A_{H,n})_s)=A_{H,n}$ canonically. The normalization on constant values makes these identifications commute with every quotient homomorphism. By the definition of completed coefficients and the sectionwise limit formula [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit], $\Gamma(s,R_H)=\varprojlim_n A_{H,n}$ as rings, with the displayed identifications respecting the limit projections.

The canonical residue map $\mathcal O_H\to\varprojlim_n A_{H,n}$ is an isomorphism. Indeed, choose integral representatives $x_n$ of a compatible family. For $m\geq n$, $|x_m-x_n|\leq|\varpi_H|^n$, with $0<|\varpi_H|<1$ by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr]. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-complete], $x_n$ converges in $H$ to some $x$. The nonarchimedean inequality gives $|x|\leq1$ and $|x-x_n|\leq|\varpi_H|^n$; the DVR factorization identifies this last ball with $\varpi_H^n\mathcal O_H$, so $x$ has the prescribed residues. An element in all these balls has absolute value zero, proving injectivity. The map is a ring homomorphism because every residue map is one. Combining with step 1 gives precisely the constant-value isomorphisms in the statement, with their quotient projections.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1), pp. 58-59; elementary completeness argument supplying the point evaluation

proof.text: Choose an $\mathcal O_E$-basis $\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_d$ of $\mathcal O_L$ by [lem-sfb-local-field-integral-basis]. The extending absolute values are compatible: restricting the absolute value of $L$ to $E$ gives the unique extending absolute value of $E$ by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-absolute-value]. Put $t=\varpi_E$, $v=\varpi_L$. The DVR factorization in $L$ gives $t=u v^e$ with $u\in\mathcal O_L^\times$ and $e\geq1$, since $0<|t|<1$. Apply [lem-pur-adic-basis-limit] with $A=\mathcal O_E$, $B=\mathcal O_L$ on the small site $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$. It gives $R_E^{\oplus d}\simeq R_L$ whose columns $b_i$ are the compatible residues of $\beta_i$. Step 2 therefore identifies $b_i(s)$ with $\beta_i$, proving the required global-basis assertion. Its coefficient map sends each $a\in\mathcal O_E$ to its constant-value image in $R_L$: this holds at each quotient projection by the explicit formula in [lem-pur-adic-basis-limit], hence in the limit. This proves compatibility with coefficient inclusions as well.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1), pp. 58-59; common basis and cofinal uniformizer-power comparison, as stated in lem-pur-adic-basis-limit

proof.text: The basis of step 3 restricts on every site object $U$ to an $R_E(U)$-basis of $R_L(U)$, with restriction-compatible coordinate maps $q_i$. Write the presheaf tensor product of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] as $P(U)=F(U)\otimes_{R_E(U)}R_L(U)$. The balanced maps $f\otimes a\mapsto(q_i(a)f)_i$ and $(f_i)_i\mapsto\sum_i f_i\otimes b_i|_U$ are inverse: on a pure tensor the second composite is $\sum_iq_i(a)f\otimes b_i=f\otimes a$, and the first composite is the identity on tuples. They commute with restrictions. Tuples of sections satisfy the sheaf axiom by gluing each coordinate, so $P\simeq F^d$ is already a sheaf. The universal property in [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] then identifies its sheafification with itself. This proves $F\otimes_{R_E}R_L\simeq F^{\oplus d}$ as $R_E$-module sheaves, by the asserted coordinate formula; it derives the sectionwise description here specifically from the finite basis.

Set $N=\Gamma(s,F)$. The formula $N\times\mathcal O_L\to\Gamma(s,F\otimes_{R_E}R_L)$, $(n,a)\mapsto n\otimes a_s$, is additive in each variable and balanced over $\mathcal O_E$, since step 3 identifies the two coefficient actions. It therefore induces $\theta_F$. It is $\mathcal O_L$-linear, because $\theta_F(n\otimes ca)=n\otimes(ca)_s=c_s(n\otimes a_s)$. The ordinary module coordinate isomorphism $N\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L\simeq N^d$ sends $n\otimes\sum_i a_i\beta_i$ to $(a_i n)_i$ and has inverse $(n_i)_i\mapsto\sum_i n_i\otimes\beta_i$; the two inverse identities are the same finite sums as in step 4. Evaluation of the sheaf coordinate isomorphism at $s$ sends $\theta_F(n\otimes\sum_i a_i\beta_i)$ to $(a_i n)_i$. Consequently $\theta_F$ is the identity between these two copies of $N^d$, hence an isomorphism with precisely the inverse in the statement (where $b_i$ on the module side denotes $\beta_i$).

source.place: Tag 03EK, sites-modules-section-tensor-product; elementary balanced-map and coordinate calculation

proof.text: For a morphism $h:F\to G$, both routes around the naturality square send $n\otimes a$ to $h_s(n)\otimes a_s$; such pure tensors generate the source, so the square commutes. The construction of $\theta_F$ used only the constant-value map and the canonical map from the presheaf tensor to its sheafification. Pure tensors also show uniqueness of a linear map with this formula. Thus two choices of basis give the same $\theta_F$, although they give different coordinate descriptions of its inverse.

source.place: Tag 03EK, sites-modules-section-tensor-product; elementary naturality and uniqueness

proof.text: The two scalar-extension functors are additive by the tensor formulas. Their underlying functors, after forgetting the extended coefficient action, are naturally the finite-power functors by steps 4 and 5. Finite powers preserve kernels and cokernels: the kernel equations hold coordinate by coordinate; maps out of a finite power are specified by their restrictions to the individual summands, so the coordinatewise cokernel has the cokernel universal property. These observations hold both for modules and for module sheaves. Restriction from $R_L$ to $R_E$ detects exactness: by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], kernels are sectionwise kernels and cokernels are sheafified sectionwise cokernels, and neither construction changes its underlying abelian sheaf on forgetting the coefficient action. The identical argument for ordinary modules uses their usual kernels and quotient modules. The finite-power descriptions therefore prove exactness of both scalar-extension functors.

source.place: Tag 03EK, sites-modules-section-tensor-product; elementary kernel and cokernel calculation for finite sums

proof.text: For a cochain complex $K^\bullet$, take $\theta_{K^j}$ in degree $j$. Naturality in step 6, applied to $d^j:K^j\to K^{j+1}$, gives $\theta_{K^{j+1}}(\Gamma(s,d^j)\otimes1)=\Gamma(s,d^j\otimes1)\theta_{K^j}$. This is exactly the chain-map identity. The degreewise inverses satisfy the inverse identity by multiplying this equation by the two inverses. Hence these maps give an isomorphism of complexes, natural in chain maps, without a boundedness condition.
